versions.provenance: 8th edition prostate TNM, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
The 8th edition staging system applies to adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The T categories shown are clinical (cT); pathologic staging has no pT1 category and pT2 is not subdivided. N is binary (N0 versus N1 for regional pelvic nodes), and M is subdivided into non-regional nodal (M1a), bone (M1b), and other visceral (M1c) metastasis.

The defining feature of 8th edition is that the prognostic stage groups combine anatomic T, N and M with the serum PSA level (ng/mL) and the Grade Group (ISUP grade derived from the Gleason score); two patients with the same T/N/M can fall into different stage groups depending on their PSA and Grade Group. The stage groups below give the anatomic T/N/M core, with the required PSA and Grade Group stated in each row's basis.

t.label: Clinically inapparent tumour that is not palpable
Tumour is an incidental histologic finding in 5% or less of tissue resected
Tumour is an incidental histologic finding in more than 5% of tissue resected
Tumour identified by needle biopsy found in one or both sides, but not palpable
Tumour is palpable and confined within the prostate
Tumour involves one-half of one side or less
Tumour involves more than one-half of one side but not both sides
Extraprostatic tumour that is not fixed and does not invade adjacent structures
Extraprostatic extension (unilateral or bilateral), including microscopic bladder neck involvement
Tumour is fixed or invades adjacent structures other than the seminal vesicles, such as the external sphincter, rectum, bladder, levator muscles, and/or pelvic wall

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed

m.label: Metastasis in other site(s), with or without bone disease

versions.regionalNodes: Pelvic nodes below the aortic bifurcation, comprising the pelvic (NOS), hypogastric (internal iliac), obturator, external iliac, and sacral (lateral, presacral, or promontory) nodes. Laterality does not affect the N category. Common iliac, para-aortic, inguinal and other nodes above the bifurcation are non-regional and are classified as M1a.
versions.histologicGrade: Grade Group (ISUP), derived from the Gleason score: Grade Group 1 = Gleason <= 6 (patterns 3 or less); Grade Group 2 = Gleason 3 + 4 = 7; Grade Group 3 = Gleason 4 + 3 = 7; Grade Group 4 = Gleason 8 (4 + 4, 3 + 5, or 5 + 3); Grade Group 5 = Gleason 9 or 10.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Acinar adenocarcinoma is by far the most common type. Variants include ductal adenocarcinoma, mucinous (colloid) carcinoma, signet-ring cell carcinoma, and small cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma. The Gleason and Grade Group systems apply to acinar and ductal adenocarcinoma.
prognosticFactors: Serum PSA level (formally incorporated into the stage group)
Grade Group / Gleason score (formally incorporated into the stage group)
Number and percentage of positive biopsy cores
Genomic classifier scores in selected cases
